proposals: PNGRB should publish one downloadable register of every ATF pipeline — airport, operator, route, length, capacity, carrier status, authorisation and commissioning dates, and annual utilisation, including tendered or proposed lines such as Bhubaneswar, Srinagar and Bhogapuram, so a line’s status does not have to be pieced together from trade press.

PNGRB should publish, for each existing dedicated ATF line, the capacity declared as common-carrier and the capacity reserved for the owner’s own use, as Indian Oil’s filing did for Bengaluru (0.16 of 0.66 million tonnes), so the reach of open access on pre-2022 lines can be checked line by line.

The Airports Authority of India should publish, for every operational airport, its ATF supply mode — pipeline, rail or road — and average daily tanker deliveries, so tanker-fed airports such as Mopa, Hirasar and Dholera can be identified from an official list rather than inferred from the absence of a pipeline proposal.

PNGRB should require each authorised ATF pipeline operator to report annual throughput and the tanker trips it replaces, so the benefit of the newer lines is measured rather than resting on a single 2008 press figure of “more than 30 tank trucks” a day at Bengaluru.
